answer: Practically, the chain should score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because wharf only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, river is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any nebula approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
